title: What Does an Architect Actually Do on Your Westchester Project?
excerpt: An architect does way more than draw pretty pictures. Here's what a licensed architect in Westchester, NY actually handles on your renovation or new construction project.
content:
When you're planning a home renovation or addition in Westchester, you might wonder what role an architect actually plays. Some homeowners think architects are optional. They're not. A good architect catches problems before they become expensive mistakes, saves you money during construction, and makes sure your house works the way you actually want to live in it.

The difference between hiring a design-build firm with a licensed architect in New York and just hiring a contractor is this: an architect is looking ahead. They're protecting you.

The Design Phase Matters

This is where an architect earns their fee. When you're planning a kitchen remodel or a second-story addition in Scarsdale or Bronxville, the architect listens to what you want, then figures out how to make it real within your budget and your house's actual constraints.

An architect in Westchester deals with a lot of existing homes. Older houses don't always cooperate. Maybe your addition in Larchmont needs to match the roofline of a 1950s colonial. Maybe your primary suite addition in Mamaroneck requires careful attention to where the utilities run. Maybe you want an open-concept kitchen but your load-bearing walls have other ideas. An architect solves these problems on paper, not on the job site where they cost ten times as much.

The architect also handles the technical drawings that your contractor needs. These aren't sketches. They're detailed, to-scale plans that show exactly what gets built, where plumbing and electrical go, what materials are specified, and how everything connects.

Permits and the Building Department

Every municipality in Westchester has its own building department. Whether you're working in Rye, New Rochelle, Hastings-on-Hudson, or Eastchester, there are permit requirements and inspections. An architect knows these processes because they work through them all the time.

The architect prepares the permit drawings and handles the submission to the local building department. They answer questions from the building inspector. They understand the code requirements that vary from one town to another. This work keeps your project legal and protects your property value. If something isn't done right, you could face fines or orders to tear out work and start over.

Construction Oversight Protects Your Investment

Here's where being a licensed general contractor in Westchester matters too. At House Architecture & Construction, Silvio M. Luca is both your architect and your general contractor. That means the same person who designed your home additions in Westchester is the one managing the crew and making sure the work matches the plans.

During construction, the architect visits the site regularly. They check quality. They review the work against the drawings. They catch mistakes early. If something unexpected happens, like old wiring inside the walls or rotted framing, the architect decides how to solve it without changing your vision or blowing the budget.

When the work is done, the architect walks through with you and the inspector to make sure everything is correct before final approval.
